topic: K1 Fix two randomized treatment-arm samples with a shared covariate marginal, positive smooth densities, and the quadratic conditional-Wasserstein partial-identification endpoint; allow smoothness and the conditional-law discrepancy to drift. K2 derive the sharp joint phase diagram for the intrinsic smoothness elbow and equality/near-equality degeneracy, including the exact null quadratic-process law and regular-to-chaos transition. K3 construct a wavelet second-order or U-statistic estimator and one confidence procedure honest across regular, null, local, and critical regimes. K4 prove matching high-frequency minimax lower bounds. Use p=1 and q_theta(y,z)=1+theta b(z)cos(2pi y), and the STAR benchmark, as witness and consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: At equality the first derivative of squared conditional W2 vanishes; its second variation is a conditional inverse-elliptic quadratic form. A wavelet estimator is therefore a degenerate quadratic statistic whose effective rank grows with resolution, while local discrepancies restore a first-order term. Existing unconditional smooth-Wasserstein null laws and fixed-entropic Sinkhorn theory do not settle this unregularized conditional frontier. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a uniform second-order expansion with controlled spectral tails and a calibration honest across null, local, smoothness-critical, and regular regimes. EARLY KILL TEST: For the cosine witness, compute the exact second variation and increasing-resolution null statistic; pivot if it tensorizes verbatim into an existing unconditional quadratic-functional theorem with no conditional calibration obstruction.

open_problems.open_problem: For randomized treatment-arm samples with a shared covariate marginal, what is the exact increasing-resolution null law of a wavelet quadratic estimator of the smooth conditional squared-Wasserstein endpoint, and how does it transition under local departures from conditional equality?

source_refs.claim: The regular root-n CLT has positive variance iff the conditional laws differ; equality is only said to be faster than root n, without a null law.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, José Blanchet, Peter Glynn

source_refs.claim: Derives null asymptotics for unconditional one-dimensional weighted L2 quantile-process functionals, a fixed unconditional benchmark rather than a conditional growing-resolution law.
source_refs.author: Eustasio del Barrio, Evarist Giné, Frederic Utzet

source_refs.excerpt: The single open question, inference at the degenerate boundary where the two arms coincide, was not solved
At equality, theta_n=0, psi_n=0, and the first-order pivot is nonnormal.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Lin et al. stop precisely where the first-order variance vanishes. The prior CausalSmith run further shows that an unregularized full-tangent Hessian can contain an infinite-dimensional identity compression, so a fixed square-summable Gaussian spectral series is not available on the full parent. Unconditional quantile-process laws have neither a covariate-indexed inverse operator nor an estimated shared marginal, while deterministic Monge–Ampère linearization does not control a wavelet projection whose rank diverges. The missing first step is a uniform conditional second-order expansion retaining the resolution-dependent inverse-elliptic spectrum and controlling its tail jointly with the local first-order term.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform second-order expansion and explicit spectral limit theorem giving the normalization and weighted-chi-square, Gaussian-chaos, Gaussian, or mixed law at equality and along local alternatives, with closed-form coefficients for q_theta(y,z)=1+theta b(z)cos(2pi y).

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact causal-bound motivation, wavelet COT estimator, regular CLT, and equality boundary at which its argument stops.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Covariates sharpen causal partial-identification bounds -> smooth densities permit wavelet COT inference -> conditional equality annihilates the first-order variance -> the missing object is the resolution-dependent second-order null and local law

method_exemplars.technique: Use quantitative harmonic approximation to replace nonlinear transport displacement by the gradient of a Poisson solution with a controlled remainder.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target Hessian is a conditional inverse-elliptic quadratic form; the transfer must make this linearization uniform in the covariate and wavelet level.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the Hoeffding decomposition and conditional CLT for changing-kernel quadratic U-statistics dominated by a degenerate second-order projection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed null statistic has a vanishing first projection and a resolution-dependent effective rank, exactly the triangular quadratic-statistic structure treated there.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its second-order causal-transport influence function and weighted chi-square equality law while tracking the loss of fixed entropic spectral damping.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It has the same causal-transport equality degeneracy, but fixed entropy makes the Hessian spectrum summable rather than resolution dependent.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp joint minimax phase diagram for the smooth conditional squared-Wasserstein causal-bound endpoint when both Hölder smoothness and distance to conditional equality drift, including matching high-frequency lower bounds in every regular, critical, local, and null zone?

source_refs.claim: Provides wavelet upper rates and a root-n CLT under a sufficient smoothness condition, but no target-specific minimax lower bound or local-to-equality rate refinement.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, José Blanchet, Peter Glynn

source_refs.claim: Proves minimax-optimal unconditional empirical-OT rates and shows separation can make OT cost estimation easier, but does not cover a conditional smooth-density equality frontier.
source_refs.author: Tudor Manole, Jonathan Niles-Weed

source_refs.claim: Establishes minimax rates for estimating a smooth density in Wasserstein loss and shows positivity changes those rates, but does not lower-bound a conditional squared-distance functional.
source_refs.author: Jonathan Niles-Weed, Quentin Berthet

source_refs.excerpt: Prove s > D/2 is necessary ... or beat it with a higher-order construction.
The sufficient thresholds s>D/2 and t_pi>Dd_X/(4s) are not claimed minimax necessary.
Choose disjoint smooth bumps, J asymp h^{-d}, and independent sign vectors z and lambda.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The known COT rate is an upper bound inherited from conditional-density estimation and a first-order stability remainder, so it need not be sharp for this scalar endpoint, especially where the derivative vanishes. Unconditional Wasserstein lower bounds perturb a whole-distribution loss, while classical quadratic-functional bounds use fixed L2 geometry. Here high-frequency alternatives are filtered by a density-dependent inverse elliptic operator and must preserve positivity and the shared covariate marginal. The adjacent rejected CausalSmith angle supplies a sign-paired fuzzy-mixture architecture, but its first proof step must be replaced by an exact evaluation of conditional-Wasserstein second variation and a balance of that quadratic separation against product-mixture affinity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A piecewise minimax RMSE formula indexed by smoothness, covariate/outcome dimension, and conditional-law discrepancy, with an attaining wavelet second-order or U-statistic estimator and matching constrained Le Cam, Assouad, or two-prior lower bounds at every phase boundary.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the exact conditional causal endpoint and the sufficient wavelet smoothness threshold whose sharpness and equality behavior remain unresolved.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Conditional transport sharpens causal bounds -> smoothness yields faster wavelet estimation -> the published threshold is only sufficient and its CLT degenerates at equality -> replace separate analyses by a sharp smoothness-by-separation minimax diagram

method_exemplars.technique: Pair wavelet upper bounds in negative Besov norms with localized packing constructions that preserve density positivity and generate Wasserstein separation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The conditional endpoint inherits negative-order geometry, but the new construction must couple both arms and integrate the inverse operator over the shared covariate law.

method_exemplars.technique: Use projection-based higher-order influence-function U-statistics and fuzzy-mixture lower bounds to balance truncation bias against degenerate variance below the first-order elbow.
method_exemplars.why_closest: At equality squared COT is locally quadratic, so its low-smoothness branch requires the same higher-order bias-variance mechanism after replacing L2 geometry by the conditional inverse-elliptic form.

method_exemplars.technique: Use smooth Brenier stability, centered-potential linearization, and semiparametric efficiency to identify the regular branch and the remainder that becomes rate determining near equality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The phase diagram must interpolate between its regular smooth-Wasserstein branch and a degenerate quadratic branch.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct a single confidence procedure for the conditional squared-Wasserstein endpoint that is honest uniformly over regular, local-to-equality, smoothness-critical, and exact-equality regimes while remaining first-order efficient at every fixed regular law?

source_refs.claim: Proves a pointwise Gaussian CLT for fixed unequal conditional laws and notes faster convergence at equality, but does not analyze triangular local alternatives or uniform cross-regime calibration.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, José Blanchet, Peter Glynn

source_refs.claim: Shows ordinary bootstrap failure under first-order degeneracy and develops corrected second-order bootstrap methods with local size control for fixed transformations.
source_refs.author: Qihui Chen, Zheng Fang

source_refs.claim: Obtains Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap approximation for incomplete U-statistics under mixed or near degeneracy, but not for a biased growing-resolution inverse-elliptic COT functional.
source_refs.author: Nils Sturma, Mathias Drton, Dennis Leung
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.excerpt: Does there exist an honest, degeneracy-adaptive confidence procedure uniformly over the variance-unrestricted parent
Sharpen the degeneracy question with an explicit local conditional-density perturbation family

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior Wald theory requires positive variance and relative remainder conditions that exclude the transition where the Hájek term is comparable to the quadratic remainder. At equality the first-order pivot is zero, while full-tangent spectral calibration is not tight. General second-order bootstrap results treat a fixed transformation with a controlled Hessian, and mixed-degeneracy incomplete-U theory injects randomization to recover Gaussianity; neither handles discrepancy drift, wavelet bias, and a growing inverse-elliptic spectrum simultaneously. A threshold selector based on an estimated first-order variance is itself unstable in the critical region, so switching naively between Wald and quadratic critical values can lose uniform coverage.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fully specified interval or test-inversion rule with a uniform coverage theorem over explicit regular, local, smoothness-critical, and null classes, pointwise semiparametric efficiency away from equality, and a nontrivial width or power guarantee at equality.

writing_exemplar.why: Its positive-variance theorem and equality remark create the two endpoints whose missing middle is the uniform local calibration problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Smooth COT yields a regular Gaussian pivot -> its variance shrinks as conditional laws approach equality -> first-order studentization fails at the boundary -> one procedure must calibrate linear and quadratic fluctuations uniformly

method_exemplars.technique: Combine its second-order one-step statistic and spectral weighted-chi-square null calibration with the regular influence-function branch.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates equality-aware causal-transport inference with fixed entropy; the target must retain honesty when regularization is absent and rank grows.

method_exemplars.technique: Use a second-order delta expansion with Babu recentering or a numerical second-derivative bootstrap to reproduce the degenerate limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Squared COT is first-order degenerate at equality, but the transfer must also accommodate nonparametric input rates and a changing Hessian.

method_exemplars.technique: Approximate both linear and kernel-variance components by a multiplier bootstrap without dividing by a collapsing Hájek variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a concrete calibration route under mixed degeneracy; the unresolved transfer is exact endpoint preservation with wavelet bias and inverse-operator estimation.

open_problems.open_problem: Which primitive covariate-direction regularization and smoothness conditions make the conditional-Wasserstein equality Hessian uniformly Hilbert-Schmidt, its spectral tail uniformly negligible, and its projected spectrum consistently estimable as wavelet resolution increases?

source_refs.excerpt: specify a covariate-direction regularization, prove a uniform Hilbert--Schmidt tail bound
regularization is what restores a square-summable spectrum
the full-tangent Hessian has an infinite-dimensional positive identity compression

open_problems.why_unsolved: The previous run establishes only a negative full-parent example: nonatomic covariate directions generate an identity compression, preventing a square-summable Gaussian series and tight fixed-rank approximation. It neither identifies a primitive class that removes this compression nor connects a wavelet cutoff to uniform eigenvalue-tail decay and estimability of the inverse-elliptic Hessian. Assuming a Hilbert-Schmidt tail or a consistent Hessian estimator would assume the load-bearing analytic step; it must be derived from conditional-density smoothness, elliptic regularity, and the covariate projection geometry.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient or sharp sufficient-condition theorem linking primitive smoothness and covariate-direction regularization to uniform Hilbert-Schmidt spectral tails, plus a consistent projected-Hessian or eigenvalue estimator with an explicit truncation-error rate.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination conditional-transport model and wavelet architecture in which primitive spectral conditions must be formulated.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Conditional COT has a smooth first-order theory -> equality exposes an inverse-elliptic Hessian -> unrestricted covariate directions destroy spectral summability -> primitive regularization conditions must restore a controllable spectrum

method_exemplars.technique: Use entropic regularization as a spectral-damping benchmark and track how the regularized Hessian and weighted chi-square law depend on the damping parameter.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows a causal-transport Hessian can have a tractable spectrum after fixed regularization; the target needs a primitive unregularized or vanishing-regularization analogue.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt elliptic Brenier stability estimates that control smooth transport potentials and quadratic remainders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The equality Hessian is inverse elliptic, so spectral decay must ultimately be derived from the same transport PDE regularity.

literature_map:
1. Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (2026, arXiv:2602.20681) are the exact anchor: wavelet COT, quadratic stability, a regular root-n CLT, and an equality remark with no null law.
2. Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (2026, AISTATS) establish direct consistent COT estimation through adapted-Wasserstein continuity, but not degeneracy-sensitive inference.
3. Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (2025, ICML, arXiv:2502.01164) replace COT by a penalty relaxation and give rates, leaving the unregularized local frontier untouched.
4. Ji, Lei, and Spector (arXiv:2310.08115) obtain robust causal-bound inference through OT duality, but address nuisance misspecification rather than equality-induced second-order degeneracy.
5. Manole, Balakrishnan, Niles-Weed, and Wasserman (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2107.12364) give smooth unconditional OT plug-in CLTs and efficiency theory.
6. Manole and Niles-Weed (2024, Annals of Applied Probability, arXiv:2106.13181) prove sharp empirical-OT rates and show separation changes difficulty, but not for conditional smooth COT.
7. Niles-Weed and Berthet (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1902.01778) give minimax smooth-density Wasserstein rates using wavelets and negative Besov geometry, not endpoint-specific COT bounds.
8. Goldman, Huesmann, and Otto (2021, CPAM, arXiv:1905.09678) quantitatively linearize Monge-Ampère transport by a Poisson equation, supporting the inverse-elliptic second variation.
9. Del Barrio, Giné, and Utzet (2005, Bernoulli) derive unconditional one-dimensional weighted-W2 null laws; there is no conditioning or growing-rank calibration.
10. Goldfeld, Kato, Nietert, and Rioux (2024, Annals of Applied Probability, arXiv:2203.00159) separate null and alternative laws for fixed Gaussian-smoothed Wasserstein distance and prove bootstrap validity.
11. Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2016, SPA, arXiv:1512.02280) prove Gaussian limits for changing-kernel degenerate quadratic U-statistics, the closest growing-rank null machinery.
12. Chen and Fang (2019, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1901.04861) show ordinary bootstrap failure under first-order degeneracy and construct second-order corrections.
13. Sturma, Drton, and Leung (2024, JRSSB, arXiv:2208.11756) give multiplier-bootstrap inference for incomplete U-statistics under mixed and near degeneracy.
14. Agarwal and Luedtke (2026, arXiv:2605.08485) derive a second-order causal Sinkhorn statistic and weighted-chi-square equality law under fixed entropy, which supplies damping absent from unregularized COT.
15. Targeted searches found no paper combining unregularized conditional W2, drifting smoothness, equality/local degeneracy, matching minimax bounds, and one honest calibration.
